clue.text: No hope for this extinct bird

blocks.note: first meaning: a plan or person with no chance of success
second meaning, taken literally: a waterfowl that is no longer alive

explanation.surface: A lament that a vanished bird species is beyond saving.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sad remark about a lost species; the idiom for a hopeless cause and a literal dead bird are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a scheme or person certain to fail, while literally it is a mallard that has died.

clue.text: Least wet from ride about street

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; jumbled
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Staying as dry as possible by riding around the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective for lacking moisture is the one with the least water in it.

clue.text: Attack Lisa as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the fodder; 'as' here does double duty with the indicator

explanation.surface: An instruction to go after a woman called Lisa according to plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone violently or with criticism is to assault them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Request made on the way out?

definitions.text: Request made on the way out?

blocks.clueFragment: Request made on the way out
blocks.note: surface reading: asking for something while leaving a room
setter's reading: on the way out means dying, so a last request before death

explanation.surface: Someone asks a favour as they head for the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A final wish voiced by someone near the end of life is one made as they depart this world.

clue.text: Dairy product sounding superior found in the kitchen

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it

indicators.note: sounding means the word for superior is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: cheese is made from milk
greater, meaning superior, said out loud

explanation.surface: A posh cheese, kept in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding superior' suggests snobbery, as if the cheese were putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: The utensil for shredding hard cheese is a standard kitchen tool, so it is located there.

clue.text: Come ashore to do kitchen work

blocks.note: first meaning: be carried onto the beach by the waves
second meaning: clean the dishes after a meal

explanation.surface: A sailor lands so as to take a turn in the galley.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood carried onto a beach is said to land this way, and the same phrasal verb means cleaning plates after eating.

clue.text: Before exercise girl has to change

indicators.note: the girl comes before the exercise, so her name leads

blocks.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A girl must alter her routine before her workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust oneself to new conditions is to alter or modify, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Time of major uprising in the main

definitions.text: Time of major uprising in the main

blocks.note: surface reading: the peak of a rebellion
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and its water rises furthest twice a day

explanation.surface: The height of a revolt, mostly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment sea levels peak in the daily cycle is when water rises most, and figuratively a peak moment.

clue.text: Gives warning of alcohol limits

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
ends are boundaries or limits

explanation.surface: A health notice on the safe ceiling for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alcohol limits' reads as drink-driving rules; split it into a drink and its boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that portends trouble foreshadows it, signalling a coming event as an omen.

clue.text: Having aroused emotions, in tears over return of French

definitions.note: describes the effect, an adjective of something stirred

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for tears is read from its end back to its start
returning means going back the way it came, so the French word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
tears as in rents in cloth; written backwards here
de is French for 'of'; written backwards here

explanation.surface: Someone moved to tears by a stirring French performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests weeping, but here it means rips, as in torn fabric. 'French' stands for a common French word, de.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspired work or person has been stirred by creative feeling, so the passive participle fits having had emotions roused.

clue.text: Where food is served in a stable environment

definitions.text: Where food is served in a stable environment

blocks.note: surface reading: a restaurant or canteen
setter's reading: a horse's feeding trough, literally inside a stable

explanation.surface: A calm, steady dining place, like a well-run café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable environment' sounds like a settled atmosphere, but it means a building for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: This trough holds hay or fodder for horses and cattle in their stalls, so animals eat there.

clue.text: Link up content -- nicer in new version

indicators.note: a new version is a rewritten form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, both words

explanation.surface: An editor's note that joining things up makes the content read better in the update.
explanation.definitionFit: To join two things together so they communicate is to connect them mutually, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Suspend medical support

blocks.note: first meaning: hang something up loosely
second meaning: a cloth loop that cradles an injured arm

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like withdrawing healthcare; the verb and the noun are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hang from straps, and as a noun it is the bandage loop holding a broken arm.

clue.text: Lots get in, possibly heading for work

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements the letters could take

blocks.note: the fodder, all three words

explanation.surface: A crowd squeezes in, perhaps on the way to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for work' looks like commuting, but heading means a title and the work is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The name printed above a piece of music heads that composition, as any title tops a work.

clue.text: Unmarried, passed over and alone

blocks.note: a single person has no spouse
handed over, gave to someone

explanation.surface: A bachelor overlooked for promotion and left on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' suggests being ignored, but it means given by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no help from anyone else means doing it by oneself, unaided.

clue.text: Has written comments from Ted to Anna translated

definitions.note: a verb phrase matching the past tense

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters change order

blocks.note: the fodder, all three words

explanation.surface: A letter from Ted to Anna has been rendered into another language with marginal notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has written comments' sounds like someone composing notes; it is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add explanatory notes in the margin, so the past form means added notes.

clue.text: Takes different view of Bible point after switching sides

indicators.note: switching means changing places, so the letters of the last word are shuffled about
after places the Bible and point behind the reworked word

blocks.note: taken as written; jumbled
NT is the New Testament
S, south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A preacher changes allegiance over a point of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching sides' looks like defecting, which suits the definition, but it only signals a jumble of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dissents disagrees with the prevailing opinion, holding an opposing position.

clue.text: Parts to which birds extend

blocks.note: surface reading: places or regions birds spread to on migration
setter's reading: the farthest points of a bird's outstretched limbs

explanation.surface: The regions into which bird populations spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost ends of feathered limbs mark the full span when a bird stretches out to fly.

clue.text: Have a ball in Dublin and see traditional entertainment

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: what people do at a ball, done in Ireland's capital
second meaning: the folk step-dance form shown on stage

explanation.surface: A tourist enjoys a night out in Dublin and catches a folk show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a ball' means have fun, but it is taken literally: a ball is a dance, held in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Step dancing from Ireland is a folk art and a stage spectacle, so it is a customary performance form.

clue.text: Away from home, manage to get further on foot

blocks.note: out means not in, away from home
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A traveller abroad tries to walk a longer distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a pursuer behind by running faster is to go beyond them while sprinting.

clue.text: Protects from light colours

blocks.note: first meaning: screens from the sun, a verb
second meaning: tints or hues, a plural noun

explanation.surface: Something guards fabrics against fading in bright sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light colours' looks like pale tones; split it, and 'light' belongs to the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means screens from sunshine; as a plural noun it means varieties of a hue.

clue.text: Wise man's naive? Perhaps a shade

blocks.note: a sage is a wise man; the 's is the verb 'is'
green means inexperienced or gullible

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that a wise man seems surprisingly innocent, perhaps a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: This greyish green, the colour of the herb's leaves, is one particular tone of colour.

clue.text: Icy danger in sea back East for diver

indicators.note: back means turned around, so the danger's word runs from end to start

blocks.note: a berg is an iceberg floating at sea; written backwards
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A warning of icebergs in eastern waters for anyone diving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a person in a wetsuit; it is a bird that dives for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterbird hunts by plunging underwater, so birdwatchers class it among diving species.

clue.text: Feel a slight trace

blocks.note: first meaning: put a hand on something
second meaning: a small amount, as in a bit of salt

explanation.surface: Sensing a faint hint of something.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means making contact by hand; as a noun it means a tiny amount or hint of something.

clue.text: Secured a form of denial

indicators.note: a form of signals the next word reshaped into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Obtaining something by a kind of refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening something with metal pins fixes it in place, so the past tense matches fastened down.

clue.text: Two boys get bullied

blocks.note: the first boy: Hector, a man's name
the second boy: Ed, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A pair of lads are picked on.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to browbeat or harangue, from the Trojan hero's name, so the past tense means intimidated.

clue.text: Family member is back before rest after mix-up

indicators.note: going back means the short word runs from its last letter to its first
a mix-up jumbles things, so the word before it is scrambled
before places the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written; written backwards
taken as written; jumbled

explanation.surface: A relative returns home before getting some rest after a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl who shares the same parents is a sibling, one of the closest relatives.

clue.text: University group makes impression on little Stuart

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after, so the first piece follows the second

blocks.note: Stu is a short form of the name Stuart
dents are impressions pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: A college crowd leaves its mark on a boy called Stuart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' suggests an effect on someone, but it means physical hollows.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergraduates and postgraduates together make up the learners enrolled at a college or campus.
